intent: Clear every over-cap billsplit Dart file, leaving only Flutter's generated Windows runner.
changes: All four lib splits use part/part of, applying the rule learned in focus_owner rather than rediscovering it - none of them needed a second attempt.

models.dart has a `library;` directive, and the splitter inserted `part` above it, which is an error: the library directive must come first. Fixed by hand, and it also revealed that the insertion had split the file's doc comment in two.

The test file split three ways, each half declaring the test binding explicitly and keeping only the imports it uses. One aliased import (`as app`) survived the first pruning pass because the filter matched exact text - worth remembering that unused-import cleanup must handle aliases.

verification.evidence: 60 passed, matching the baseline measured before any edit.

verification.command: flutter analyze, compared against the same command in a detached worktree at HEAD
verification.evidence: 4 issues after, 4 issues before - all pre-existing unnecessary_unawaited infos. Comparing against a worktree rather than assuming a clean baseline is what showed the intermediate run's 7 issues were 3 of my own making, including one real error.
Only windows/runner/win32_window.cpp remains, and it is Flutter-generated scaffolding: editing it would be undone the next time the Windows target is regenerated.

risks: part/part of puts the split files in one library namespace, so two parts cannot declare the same private name. Not an issue today, but invisible until it collides.
win32_window.cpp stays over the cap. It is vendored Flutter scaffolding, so the honest options are an exemption or leaving it; splitting it would be undone by `flutter create`.
rollback: git revert the commit; the five originals return and the seven new files disappear.
After rollback, re-run flutter test and expect 60 passed.
